summary.patient_symptoms_summary: You reported recent fatigue, "a little bit of flap," and very dry skin. You had one side of your thyroid removed about one month ago for a tumor that you described as a "good one" but getting too big. You came today to review your blood test results and ask what to do.
summary.doctor_advice: Start thyroid replacement medication at a very low dose. Take it on an empty stomach every day, ideally at the same time, best first thing in the morning with a glass of water (around 7:30–8:00 am). Watch for signs of too much thyroid: your heart beating very fast, feeling very anxious, feeling really bad or really stressed; if that happens, seek urgent help or go to the hospital. The doctor explained that thyroid hormones regulate metabolism and that too much can cause arrhythmia, a very fast heartbeat, and make you feel anxious or stressed. A follow-up review was suggested in three months to see how the medication has helped.
red_flags: Heart beating really fast while on the tablets
Feeling very anxious while on the tablets
Feeling really bad or really stressed while on the tablets
